So I'm trying to get my WiFi set up on my laptop and I'm struggling a bit. I installed the latest i386 debian distribution using the DVD disk. I didn't have my ethernet connected during installation and I selected KDE as my GUI. I've tried to RTFM but every time I run into an issue and look it up I get wildly different recommendations on what to try to fix it.

I started off reading this page: https://wiki.debian.org/WiFi

First problem I ran into is it says it can't find an installation candidate for "wicd". What does that mean?
Second I was curious how I could determine if Linux already found and installed my WiFi driver?
Third for the moment I decided to assume it hadn't installed my driver and I believe I need the Broadcom driver. However running apt-get install firmware-b43-installer b43-fwcutter tells me that neither package can be found. I did find one of the packages here: https://packages.debian.org/jessie/firmware-b43-installer and I took a look at synaptic package manager's repositories but I couldn't figure out what to do next?

Apologies if these seem like dumb questions. I really am trying here. :(

EDIT:

So with /u/thantik 's help I was able to figure out the issues. I suspect that since I did not have an internet connection when installing Debian my /etc/apt/sources.list file didn't get some repos added and was just relying on the DVD. There were some commented out repos in the file which I realized were pointing to jessie-update but I believe I needed a repo for jessie aside from the DVD. So I added the following lines:

deb [http://ftp.debian.org/debian/](http://ftp.debian.org/debian/) jessie contrib main
deb-src [http://ftp.debian.org/debian/](http://ftp.debian.org/debian/) jessie contrib main

Once I saved the file I ran apt-get update again and then the command to install the Wifi drivers worked.

EDIT 2:

Success! I am now posting from my WiFi connection. After I installed the drivers I ran ifconfig -a to see if wlan0 had appeared. It hadn't yet so I rebooted and ran the command again and success! wlan0 was now present. From there I used the "Network Connections" utility that was already installed to define a Wireless network. Entered in my SSID and Wifi security information and it fired up instantly. :) Woohoo!
